transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-01
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Laura Chen (Redwood AE), Markus Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Cartwheel Head of Search), Darren Lowe (Cartwheel SRE), Marta Ruiz (Cartwheel ML Eng)

Summary: initial discovery focused on embedding+rerank for product personalization at high qps, exploring hosted vs dedicated vs private, vector DB integration (they use a homegrown fanout today), dimensionality tradeoffs, and a potential 2-week hosted perf pilot.

Topics: embeddings dims, vector DB sync, fanout vs cascade rerank, throughput and tail latency, VPC/KMS constraints, pilot success criteria.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Laura Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Laura from Redwood. Quick intro — Markus is our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:05] Priya Nair: Hi Laura. Good, thanks. I'm Priya — I own search and recommendations at Cartwheel. We've been looking to move from our in-house nearest neighbor fanout to something more predictable, and want to understand where Redwood fits.
[00:13] Darren Lowe: Darren here, SRE. I'll be focused on networking, VPC and operational concerns.
[00:17] Marta Ruiz: And Marta, ML eng. We'll be responsible for evaluation and data.
[00:20] Markus Patel: Great, thanks. Quick agenda: clarify current infra and qps, discuss embedding design (dimensionality + model), talk hosting choices (hosted/dedicated/private) and typical tradeoffs, and identify next steps for a perf pilot. Sound okay?
[00:30] Priya: Yep. To start, our current traffic for product personalization endpoints is around 120 qps at peak, spiky for holiday windows up to 300 qps for short bursts. Typical latency SLO for the end user is 200 ms P95 for the whole request, which includes retrieval, rerank, and business logic. Retrieval is currently a fanout to our in-house vector store across three regions then a rerank model to re-score top 100.
[00:50] Markus: Helpful. When you say rerank top 100, what's the model size and is it latency-sensitive?
[00:55] Priya: The reranker is a cross-encoder — it's BERT-small-ish, does batch rerank offline but for online we do a light cross-encoder that costs ~35 ms per candidate on CPU in our infra, so we only rerank top 20 in the hot path today.
[01:12] Laura: Makes sense. Typical architecture choices we see: keep a lightweight embedding retrieval in the hot path and then do a heavier cross-encoder for the top-k. Redwood supports both the retrieval and rerank step — you can run the embedding model in Redwood Hosted to produce vectors and then either use our outbound call to a managed VDB or keep your DB and call Redwood for rerank.
[01:29] Darren: We have strict egress and a corporate firewall. Private deployment is something we might consider as well. Also KMS keys: keys must be customer-managed HSM backed.
[01:38] Markus: Understood. For KMS we integrate with customer KMS/HSM for Private and some Dedicated setups, and Hosted supports Bring-Your-Own-Key in the control plane with envelope encryption. There are some differences in who holds the key material and at-rest access patterns.
[01:52] Marta: On embedding dims, we've historically used 768 dims from a distil model but are experimenting with 256 and compact representations. Curious how Redwood routes hybrid top-k or supports fanout.
[02:03] Markus: Two common approaches: 1) high-dim vectors on the VDB and a local dimension-reduction for throughput; 2) compact embeddings for high-qps retrieval with an accuracy/econ tradeoff. For fanout we support routing policies — you can do multi-tiered retrieval (coarse first, then narrow) or a cascade where Redwood returns candidates and we run the cross-encoder in our Dedicated runtime.
[02:22] Priya: Could you clarify the performance implications? If we move more to Redwood Hosted for embeddings and maybe a rerank on Redwood Dedicated, what should we expect on end-to-end latency?
[02:32] Markus: For hosted embeddings generation we see sub-10ms per embed on smaller models (e.g., 768-dists) with batching. The vector DB lookup latency depends on your index and hosting — managed VDB like Pinecone or Milvus can be 5-20ms for topk10 depending on shard layout and region. If you then send top20 to a cross-encoder in Redwood Dedicated GPU pool, you can add ~20-40ms depending on the model and batch. So end-to-end retrieval + rerank P95 in the 80-180 ms range is possible, but depends on network egress and per-request fanout.
[03:01] Priya: Our tail is the problem — the fanout to three regions contributes a lot of variability.
[03:07] Darren: And cold start of ephemeral services sometimes spikes. We need predictable tail behavior.
[03:11] Laura: That's where Dedicated and Private shine — you pin capacity, reduce network hops, and can colocate model serving near the VDB. We also have caching for common prefixes/KV cache that reduces calls for repetitive patterns.
[03:25] Marta: On dimensionality, curious if there are recommendations: we need high recall for personalization but also want to reduce vector storage and lookup time. Is there a recommended embed dim for product catalogs?
[03:36] Markus: For product catalogs with many SKUs, we often recommend 256 as a starting point if you use a reranker downstream. If you want retrieval-only relevance without rerank, 512-768 tends to perform better. But with a cascade rerank you can get away with 128-256 and still maintain quality while improving throughput/cost.
[03:55] Priya: We run a daily update pipeline that writes 5M product vectors across three regions. That's a lot of ingestion — how would Redwood handle that write throughput?
[04:05] Markus: For high-volume ingest we recommend Dedicated capacity or Private where we can offer sustained throughput and configurable autoscaling. Hosted can handle bursts but sustained multi-million writes per day is typically better with Dedicated. We also offer shard-aware sync to push updates in parallel and avoid reindexing hotspots.
[04:22] Darren: What about consistency models? We can't afford long staleness for pricing or stock data.
[04:27] Markus: We support configurable TTL and near-real-time sync strategies. For strict freshness, Private/Dedicated with direct VPC peering is typical — you can push updates to a hot cache and maintain tight consistency. Hosted will have slightly higher propagation delays but usually within seconds, depending on index type.
[04:43] Priya: On the vector DB side, we've been using a mixture of L2 and inner-product indices. We'll likely use an IVF+PQ for cost. Any guidance on that with Redwood?
[04:52] Markus: Excellent — IVF+PQ is common for storage and cost tradeoff. Redwood's routing can translate query vectors and handle similarity metric compatibility. If you choose aggressive PQ for storage, you'll want a stronger reranker downstream to recover precision.
[05:05] Marta: Are there any built-in tooling to help pick dims and PQ params?
[05:09] Laura: Yes — Redwood Optimize will run sample sweeps on your workload and give recommended dims, PQ settings, and batching configs to meet latency targets within cost constraints. We can run an initial sweep as part of a pilot.
[05:21] Darren: Network question: If we go Hosted but keep the VDB in our cloud account, will Redwood call into it? That might require firewall exceptions.
[05:29] Markus: We support both outbound calls (Redwood calls your VDB over egress) and a hybrid connector where you deploy a small proxy in your VPC (connectors). Many customers prefer the connector to avoid opening broad firewall ranges.
[05:40] Priya: We'd prefer not to open wide egress; we'll want the connector approach or a private deployment.
[05:45] Laura: Noted. For the pilot, we can propose a hosted->connector flow: Redwood Hosted for embed generation and rerank, connector for VDB access, and a small dedicated rerank instance if needed to meet P95.
[05:58] Priya: Pricing check — at high throughput, how does Dedicated compare to Hosted for embeddings and rerank?
[06:05] Laura: Typically, Dedicated has a higher base cost (reserved capacity) but lower per-token/per-embed compute unit and predictable tail latency. Hosted is pay-as-you-go and is cheaper at low to moderate sustained usage. For your peak pattern with sustained high ingest, Dedicated often wins on unit economics once you commit. We can model that in a one-pager after we see your sample throughput.
[06:25] Marta: On the rerank model itself, if we were to offload the heavier cross-encoder to Redwood, how does model versioning and rollout work? We need to run A/B and canary.
[06:34] Markus: Redwood Console supports model version pinning, canary rollout, A/B traffic split and automatic fallback if a model underperforms. You can also keep a shadow model for evaluation.
[06:44] Darren: Security — audit logs, SSO, RBAC — do you have SOC2?
[06:49] Laura: Yes, SOC2 Type II, and we do ISO27001 in certain regions. We have fine-grained RBAC in the Console, SSO with SAML/OIDC, and audit logs exported to customer buckets or SIEM. We'll send the security pack.
[07:01] Priya: Great. For the pilot success criteria: we want to see P95 request end-to-end under 200ms, 95% recall at top20 compared to current baseline, and no more than 2s of index downtime during updates. Does that sound reasonable?
[07:12] Markus: That maps well to what we can measure. We'll instrument token-level and route-level metrics and share dashboards.
[07:18] Marta: One operational question — how do you handle KV cache invalidation for product updates? Some products toggle visibility quickly.
[07:24] Markus: We expose cache-control and invalidation APIs. For inventory toggles we recommend a hot-update path that invalidates the product ID in the cache and pushes a delta to the VDB index. This is easier with Dedicated/Private since you control the peering.
[07:39] Priya: Could we do an initial proof-of-concept only on a single category? Say footwear, roughly 150k items to start?
[07:46] Laura: Absolutely — scoped pilot on a category is typical. We can run a 2-week pilot with a 1M document subset if you want broader signals.
[07:53] Darren: For connector deployment — what's the operational footprint? We'll prefer something that doesn't need full-time ops.
[07:59] Markus: Connectors are lightweight: a small fleet of containers (k8s) or a VM with a stable egress endpoint. They require limited maintenance — we provide Helm charts and documented runbooks.
[08:10] Priya: Any traps you've seen in migrations?
[08:13] Markus: Two big ones: underestimating QPS headroom for fanout, and over-compressing vectors without a reranker. Both can cause quality regressions or tail spikes. The sample sweep from Optimize helps avoid those.
[08:25] Marta: On evaluation, we have a labeled set of 5k queries; would Redwood run the eval to compare dims and PQ params?
[08:31] Laura: Yes — we can run an evaluation harness, compare recall/precision at various dims and PQ configs, and produce a recommendation sheet. We'll need your labeled set and sample traffic.
[08:40] Priya: Timeline question — if we kick off the pilot next week, how quickly can we get results?
[08:45] Laura: If you provide the sample dataset and credentials for connector within 3 business days, we can stand up the pilot in about 72 hours and start collecting metrics. Two weeks of run time should give statistical significance for latency and recall.
[08:58] Darren: Regarding compliance: can logs be pushed to our SIEM with PII redaction?
[09:03] Markus: Yes, we can push anonymized transcripts and logs with configurable redaction rules. For PII, we have field-level redaction and token filters.
[09:13] Priya: Okay — sounds good. Regarding competitors, we've also looked at Pinecone and Milvus and a couple of managed rerank options from a few cloud providers. Curious about migration friction.
[09:24] Laura: Pinecone is straightforward for managed vector DB access — many customers pair Redwood with Pinecone; Milvus often needs more ops and tuning. Our value-add is the end-to-end routing, cost optimizations, and fallback policies.
[09:36] Marta: Quick technical— for rerank batching, how do you handle sequences of variable length? We have some long product descriptions occasionally.
[09:42] Markus: We use dynamic batching and sequence bucketing; on GPU (Dedicated) that's efficient. We also offer quantized models for faster runtimes if you can accept a small accuracy hit.
[09:53] Priya: A nit: can we keep model artifacts in our repo for audit?
[09:57] Laura: For Private deployments yes; for Hosted we maintain artifacts but can provide hashes and provenance. Dedicated can be configured to use customer-managed model registries.
[10:08] Darren: Any SLA numbers for Dedicated?
[10:11] Markus: Yes, Dedicated comes with an SLA for availability and latency SLOs that we can include in the commercial agreement.
[10:17] Priya: Great. Let's recap next steps.
[10:20] Laura: Recap: 1) Cartwheel to share sample dataset (150k footwear subset and labeled queries) and top-k requirements; 2) Markus will configure a hosted->connector pilot and run an Optimize sweep; 3) Redwood to send security pack and pricing sketch for Hosted vs Dedicated; 4) schedule technical deep-dive week of 2026-10-12. Anything to add?
[10:38] Priya: That's it. We'll also include Darren's firewall/KMS constraints in the notes.
[10:42] Darren: I'll send those by Tuesday.
[10:44] Marta: I'll provide the labeled set and the query distribution.
[10:46] Laura: Perfect. I'll follow up with the security docs and a pilot kickoff doc this afternoon. Markus will own the perf matrix deliverable.
[10:52] Priya: Thanks all.
[10:54] Laura: Thanks, everyone — we'll follow up via email.

--- End transcript ---

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings around product names (e.g., sometimes "connector" transcribed as "connectorn"), filler words kept. Some speaker labels consolidated where the automated tool could not distinguish tightly.
